subject: SIG questionnaire: follow-up and evidence for access controls
messages:
From: James Taylor <j.taylor@acmelogistics.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Cc: sig-requests@acmelogistics.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: access controls details

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the initial SIG bundle earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our security team on access controls (SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and MFA) — we need concise answers + evidence files by EOD Friday if possible. Specific asks: 

- Confirm whether Redwood supports SCIM v2 for automated user provisioning and provide a sample provisioning payload.
- Provide the SSO/SAML metadata (IdP/SP) and a diagram showing how SAML assertions map to internal roles.
- Explain RBAC model: which built-in roles exist, how custom roles are created, and an example least-privilege role for an engineer who needs read-only model telemetry.
- Describe MFA enforcement (which users, enforced at IdP or app-level).

If easier, send answers in a short doc and attach the sample artifacts. We may need screenshots of the console showing role assignment and SCIM logs.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — James
Security Engineer | Acme Logistics

From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
To: James Taylor <j.taylor@acmelogistics.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: access controls details

Hi James — thanks, we'll get this over. High-level answers below; attaching a spreadsheet with the fuller SIG responses and three evidence files (SIG_Access_Controls.xlsx, sso-saml-arch.png, scim-provisioning-sample.json). See details: 

1) SCIM provisioning:
- We support SCIM 2.0 with user and group endpoints (PATCH/PUT/POST).
- Provisioning runs over mTLS with bearer tokens; provisioning events are logged to the audit stream.
- Attached: scim-provisioning-sample.json (sample user create payload) + audit log excerpt in the spreadsheet.

2) SSO / SAML:
- Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC. Customers can upload IdP metadata or download SP metadata.
- We map SAML attributes (email, uid, groups) to internal RBAC roles via a mapping table in the admin console.
- Attached: sso-saml-arch.png (diagram) and the SP metadata download link in the spreadsheet.

3) RBAC and least privilege:
- Built-in roles: Owner, Admin, Billing Admin, Developer, ReadOnly.
- Custom roles: admin UI + API to create role with fine-grained permissions (models:read, models:write, telemetry:read, infra:manage).
- Example least-privilege role for engineer: {\"name\": \"Telemetry Reader\", \"perms\": [\"telemetry:read\", \"models:read\"]} — see spreadsheet for JSON snippet.

4) MFA:
- MFA is enforced at the IdP for SAML/OIDC customers; for hosted accounts using Redwood identity, we enforce TOTP-based MFA for all accounts with console access.

Next steps: Dev (cc'd) will attach the SCIM payload and a short RBAC export showing the example role. Let us know if you also need console screenshots of the role assignment flow.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.example.com
To: James Taylor <j.taylor@acmelogistics.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: access controls details

James — attaching the raw files you requested. Quick notes on the SCIM sample and RBAC export: 

- Attachment: scim-provisioning-sample.json — sample POST /scim/v2/Users payload we send when creating an account via SCIM. Fields include userName, name.familyName, name.givenName, active, emails and groups attribute that maps to group membership.
- Provisioning logs: we include request/response IDs, timestamp, requester (service account id). We redact PII in exports; raw logs can be provided under NDA.
- RBAC export: see sheet tab "rbac_example" in SIG_Access_Controls.xlsx — shows built-in roles and the custom "Telemetry Reader" role JSON.

Inline example (redacted) — Telemetry Reader role: 
{
  "role_id": "role_tr_002",
  "name": "Telemetry Reader",
  "permissions": ["telemetry:read", "models:read"],
  "scope": "org:12345"
}

If you need a video walkthrough of the role assignment flow we can record one; otherwise the spreadsheet should be sufficient for SIG reviewers.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Product Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: James Taylor <j.taylor@acmelogistics.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.example.com, sig-requests@acmelogistics.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: access controls details

Kimberly / Dev — got the spreadsheet and attachments, thanks. Two quick clarifications from our reviewers: 

- For SCIM: can you confirm whether group membership changes trigger push notifications to the SP or if they are only visible on periodic syncs? We need to know how quickly group->role changes take effect for account deprovisioning.
- For RBAC: does the Telemetry Reader role allow any access to token-level logs or only aggregated metrics? Our compliance bar disallows token-level exposure to non-admins.

If you can reply with short, specific answers and (if available) a console screenshot of the group-to-role mapping, that would be helpful.

Thanks — James

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: James Taylor <j.taylor@acmelogistics.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, dev_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: access controls details

James — quick follow-up: 

- SCIM propagation: group membership changes pushed by the IdP are processed in near-real time. We consume SCIM events via a webhook-backed worker that applies changes immediately; typical propagation is <60s in normal conditions. If the customer's IdP uses bulk sync, the timing follows their sync window. We included a short log excerpt in the spreadsheet showing a group removal and an immediate deprovisioning event.

- Telemetry Reader scope: the Telemetry Reader role grants telemetry:read and models:read which map to aggregated metrics and per-model usage histograms only. It does NOT grant access to raw token payloads or token-level logs. Token-level logs are restricted to Admin and Owner roles and are recorded in audit trails.

Attached is a console screenshot (tab in SIG_Access_Controls.xlsx) showing a group-to-role mapping entry and the RBAC UI where you can toggle permission bits. If you need an exported policy that explicitly denies token-level log access for the role, say the word and we will produce it as a signed artifact.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Security Manager | Redwood Inference
